question.text: Will the Global Protest Tracker report any protests in India or Pakistan with 10,000+ participants starting in November or December 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if the [Global Protest Tracker](https://carnegieendowment.org/features/global-protest-tracker) reports a protest in India or Pakistan with a peak size of 10,000 or more, with a start date after October 31, 2026 and before January 1, 2027.

research:
I've finished the research and am writing up the findings now.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-28 (fetched): The [Global Protest Tracker](https://carnegieendowment.org/features/global-protest-tracker) says "Last updated: September 9, 2026". Its newest entries overall are from August 2026. In the text I scraped (about 400k of 512k characters), each entry showed only a title, a month and year, and a trigger. I could not see any peak-size field, so I could not check sizes for any India or Pakistan entry. They probably sit in expandable or interactive fields.
- Latest India entries: Exam scandal protests (Jun 2026), Women's quota protest (Apr 2026), Protests against the war in Iran and a strike against the U.S.-India trade deal (both Feb 2026), Ladakh (Sep 2025), Voter roll revision (Aug 2025), Bharat Bandh (Jul 2025).
- Latest Pakistan entries: Fuel price protests (Aug 2026), 2026 Kashmir protests (Jun 2026), Protests against the war in Iran (Mar 2026), 2025 Kashmir protests (Oct 2025), PECA amendment protests (Jan 2025).
- Timing risk: the tracker was about 7 weeks behind when I checked. The question resolves around 2027-01-01, so a protest that starts in Nov or Dec 2026 may not be added before resolution.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The window opens 2026-11-01, and as of 2026-10-28 no qualifying entry can exist.
- The October 2026 events (the "Cockroach" protests in Delhi and the PTI march around the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency) started before November. If the tracker adds them, they would most likely carry an Oct 2026 start date and would not count.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-28: Thousands of students protested in Muzaffarabad, Pakistan-administered Kashmir, over the killing of 10-year-old Shayan Azhar in Bagh district. The source is partisan and I did not verify it. Because this started in October, it could be logged as Oct 2026, or folded into the existing "2026 Kashmir protests" entry. [OpIndia](https://www.opindia.com/news-updates/justice-for-shayan-azhar-thousands-of-students-hit-the-streets-in-pojk-over-the-killing-of-a-10-year-old-boy-by-pakistani-forces/)
- 2026-10-27: The Campaign for the Right to Protest in Bengaluru (about 100 people) gave the government a Nov 26 deadline and threatened city-wide civil disobedience on Nov 28. [New Indian Express](https://www.newindianexpress.com/cities/bengaluru/2026/Oct/27/group-sets-govt-nov-26-deadline-to-lift-bengaluru-protest-venue-curbs-warns-of-mass-stir)
- 2026-10-26: A mahapanchayat in Rohtak backed a Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM) farmers' march to Delhi on Nov 26. Demands are a legal guarantee of minimum support prices (MSP), debt relief, withdrawal of the labour codes, and a halt to India-US trade deal talks. No expected turnout was given. [Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/rohtak-mahapanchayat-announces-protests-backs-nov-26-delhi-march/)
- 2026-10-19: A Guardian opinion piece says the Delhi "carnival of protest" has shaken Modi like nothing before. [Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/oct/19/india-protest-delhi-cockroach-narendra-modi)
- 2026-10-10 to 10-13: Police cracked down on the Cockroach Janta Party protests against the voter roll revision and the election chief. About 2,000 to 2,500 people were detained, then the leaders were released and pledged more protests. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/10/indias-cockroach-leaders-detained-new-delhi-in-lockdown); [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/india-cockroach-protests-modi-voter-list-revision-rcna603149); [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/leaders-from-indias-cockroach-movement-released-from-detention-pledge-to-hold-more-protests)
- 2026-10-11: Pakistan imposed emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa while a PTI march for Imran Khan's release was underway. Chief Minister Afridi was reportedly arrested. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/11/pakistan-imposes-emergency-rule-in-khyber-pakhtunkhwa); [ThePrint](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-ousts-pti-govt-imposes-emergency-in-khyber-pakhtunkhwa-as-party-marches-for-jailed-imran/3068557/)
- After 2026-10-11: PTI says it held back from immediate protests to protect its workers, but says it has not given up the struggle. It is challenging the emergency in the Peshawar High Court. [Dawn](https://dawn.com/news/2040067)
- I found no announced PTI mass protest date for Nov or Dec 2026.

## 4. Base rates
- Tracker entries starting in Nov or Dec, by year:
  - 2023: one Pakistan entry (Baloch march, Nov 2023) and two India entries (Dec 2023)
  - 2024: two India entries (Mosque survey and Adani protests, Nov 2024)
  - 2025: none for India or Pakistan
  - Earlier: Pakistan Nov 2017 and Nov 2018; India Dec 2019
- So in roughly 5 of the last 9 Nov-Dec windows, at least one India or Pakistan entry started in the window. I could not check how many of those had a peak size of 10,000 or more.
- Recent pace: about 12 India or Pakistan entries across Jan 2025 to Aug 2026, roughly 0.6 a month for the two countries combined.
- Pakistan's PTI marches in Nov 2024 were large (tens of thousands), yet I did not see a separate Nov 2024 PTI entry. They may have been folded into the existing "Protest for the release of Imran Khan" (May 2024) entry. Continuing movements tend to be absorbed into older entries in this way, which matters for a new start date being recorded.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question. The nearest is Polymarket "India strike on Pakistan by Dec 31, 2026" at 7.5% Yes, which has only an indirect link.
- A [Manifold market](https://manifold.markets/BlueDragon/in-what-country-will-the-next-mass) on the tracker exists, but it is about 2024. I found no current market or expert forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-26: SKM farmers' march to Delhi (Constitution Day). Past SKM mobilisations, such as Nov 2020, were huge. [Tribune](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/rohtak-mahapanchayat-announces-protests-backs-nov-26-delhi-march/)
- 2026-11-28: Threatened civil disobedience in Bengaluru if venue restrictions are not lifted.
- Ongoing: The Cockroach movement's pledged further protests on the voter roll revision.
- Ongoing: PTI's response to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency, the Peshawar High Court ruling, and possible mobilisation around Imran Khan. The Nov 24 anniversary of the 2024 march falls in the window.
- Ongoing: Unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir over the Shayan Azhar killing.
- Tracker updates: whether Carnegie updates before about Jan 1, 2027, and whether it logs new Nov or Dec movements as separate entries, are key uncertainties. The last update was Sep 9, 2026.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The question resolves around 2027-01-01, about 9 weeks from now. For Yes, the Carnegie Global Protest Tracker must list a new India or Pakistan protest with a start date in November or December 2026 and a peak size of 10,000 or more. It must also add that entry before the question resolves.

(b) Status quo: there is no such entry, and the tracker was last updated on Sep 9, 2026, about 7 weeks behind. October movements, such as the Cockroach protests in Delhi and the PTI march around the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency, would carry October start dates and would not count. If nothing changes, this resolves No.

(c) Base rate: in about 5 of the last 9 Nov-Dec windows, at least one India or Pakistan entry started in the window. Applying the 10,000+ size filter probably leaves about 35-45%. Large entries are common for India, such as bandhs and farmer protests. That figure ignores the problem of the tracker's lag.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The SKM farmers' march to Delhi on Nov 26 (Tribune, 2026-10-26) has the potential for very large turnout.
- The Cockroach movement pledged further protests (PBS, mid-October).
- PTI is mobilising after the KP emergency (2026-10-11), and the Nov 24 anniversary falls in the window.
- There is unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir (2026-10-28).
- The political temperature in both countries is unusually high.

Evidence for No:
- The tracker lags by about 7 weeks (last updated Sep 9). A late-November protest may not appear by Jan 1, and a December one even less likely.
- Continuing movements are often folded into older entries. The Nov 2024 PTI marches apparently went into the May 2024 entry. The SKM march could be folded into the Feb 2026 trade-deal strike entry.
- PTI has said it is holding back on immediate protests.

(e) No scenario: The SKM march draws large crowds but is logged under an existing entry, or it is only added in a January update. The PTI and Cockroach actions are treated as continuations of October entries. The result is No.

Yes scenario: Carnegie updates in mid-December. It adds a "Farmers' march to Delhi (Nov 2026)" entry, or a new PTI protest wave, with a peak size of 10,000 or more.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 40% that a qualifying protest occurs and is logged as a new entry. Heightened tensions push that to about 45%. I then multiply by about 0.5 for the chance the tracker adds it before resolution, given the lag and the late-November timing. That gives about 22%.

Probability: 22%

(a) About 9 weeks remain, with resolution around 2027-01-01. For Yes, the Carnegie Global Protest Tracker must list an India or Pakistan protest with a start date between Nov 1 and Dec 31, 2026 and a peak size of 10,000 or more. It must also add that entry before the question is checked.

(b) If nothing changed, the answer is No. The tracker was last updated Sep 9, 2026, its newest entries are from August, and no qualifying entry can exist yet.

(c) Base rate: in about 5 of the last 9 Nov-Dec windows, at least one India or Pakistan entry started in the window. That is roughly 55%, before applying the 10,000+ size filter. Many India and Pakistan entries are large, so with the filter it is perhaps 40-50%. The real constraint is publication lag. The tracker runs about 7 weeks behind, so a protest starting in late November or in December probably would not appear by Jan 1. Correcting for lag, the base rate for "qualifying and visible by Jan 1" is perhaps 15-25%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- India is in heavy turmoil: the Cockroach movement in October 2026 had 2,000-2,500 detained and pledged further protests.
- The SKM farmers' march to Delhi is set for Nov 26, and SKM mobilisations have been huge before.
- In Pakistan, the PTI is aggrieved by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa emergency (Oct 11), and the Nov 24 anniversary of its 2024 march falls in the window.
- There is unrest in Pakistan-administered Kashmir (Oct 28).

Evidence for No:
- The tracker lagged about 7 weeks as of Oct 28.
- Continuing movements tend to be folded into older entries. The October Cockroach and PTI movements would carry October start dates.
- The PTI has no announced Nov-Dec mass protest date.
- The Nov 26 march is late in the window relative to the lag.
- The 2025 Nov-Dec window had no entries at all.

(e) No scenario: the farmers' march happens but Carnegie's December update covers only through October or early November. Alternatively, Cockroach and PTI activity is logged under its October start dates. Either way, nothing qualifying appears by Jan 1.

Yes scenario: a new mass mobilisation in early November, such as a PTI march or a fresh protest wave in India, draws tens of thousands. Carnegie updates in mid-December and lists it with a peak size above 10,000.

(f) The chance that a qualifying protest occurs is about 50-55%. The chance it is logged as a new entry with a Nov-Dec start and published before resolution is about 40%. That gives roughly 20-22%. I add a little in case resolution is checked somewhat after Jan 1.

Probability: 22%

That puts the chance of a qualifying entry eventually existing at roughly 35-40%. The tracker typically lags events by 1-3 months, so only part of that would be visible by Jan 1. Probability: 22%
